why.terrace: Sector B (south stand) leads songs, choreos and pyro; Bulgaria's most popular club (31% in a UEFA study)
why.city: Sofia's 'blue' half, sharing the capital with CSKA; national following
why.voice: Fan association 'Levski for the Levskars' holds 10%; fans raised 2.6m BGN in 2020 to save the club
why.conscience: UEFA fined Levski EUR 40,000 in Aug 2023 for supporters' ethnic and political chanting v Shkupi
why.ground: Georgi Asparuhov (17,688), older ground in Suhata Reka, partly rebuilt 2016
why.contender: 2025-26 Bulgarian champions (27th title), 2022 cup; Bulgaria's second-most decorated club
why.rituals: Anthem 'Samo Levski shampion' (1999), Sector B choreos; known in Bulgaria
why.stewardship: Investment banker Atanas Bostandjiev (Gemcorp) took majority control Apr 2026 from ex-player Nasko Sirakov

why.terrace: Union Bhoys on the all-standing Tribune Est; atmosphere widely praised in Belgium
why.city: Neighbourhood club of Saint-Gilles/Forest and the Marolles in Brussels, sharing the city with Anderlecht
why.voice: Privately owned; no formal supporter power found (estimate)
why.conscience: 'Anti-fascist Unionist for Life' unofficial motto; progressive, anti-racist support; nothing notable sanctioned found
why.ground: Joseph Marien (9,400), compact 1920s ground in Forest park
why.contender: 2024-25 Belgian champions (first in 90 years), cups 2024 and 2026, 2025-26 runners-up
why.rituals: 'Vamos a la playa' goal and full-time song, 'Le chant des goals' anthem
why.stewardship: Alex Muzio majority owner and chairman since 2023 (Tony Bloom's co-investor; Bloom had majority 2018-23); analytics-led model
why.women: Estimate; women's team not covered in sources opened
why.intensity: Direct, high-energy, set-piece-strong sides that won titles on a small budget (estimate)

why.terrace: Bad Blue Boys (1986) on the north stand; well known across the Balkans
why.city: Zagreb's main club and Croatia's most supported
why.voice: Non-profit members' association with one member one vote, but long captured by the Mamic era; supporter group Zajedno za Dinamo campaigned against it
why.conscience: BBB linked to far-right imagery; 100+ members detained after the fatal stabbing of an AEK fan in Athens (2023); UEFA racism sanctions 2013 and 2019
why.ground: Maksimir (35,123 per club page), ageing, long-delayed rebuild, often far from full
why.rituals: BBB choreos and the Eternal Derby v Hajduk; known regionally
why.stewardship: Members' association, no shares; Zvonimir Boban president; Zdravko Mamic convicted of corruption (2018)
why.women: Women's team is a separate club (ZNK Dinamo Zagreb)

why.terrace: Main ultras Gate 9 quit the football team in 2018 to found PAC Omonia 29M; remaining support still sizeable
why.city: Nicosia's working-class, left-leaning 'people's club', sharing the city with APOEL
why.voice: Members voted in 2018 to hand football to a private company; fan control ended
why.conscience: Founded by left-wing players expelled from APOEL; left/working-class identity; nothing notable sanctioned found
why.ground: Shares the 22,859-seat New GSP with APOEL; own 16,000-seat ground planned for 2028-29
why.contender: 2025-26 Cypriot champions (22nd title), 2021 title, cups 2022 and 2023
why.rituals: 1971 anthem, shamrock and green-white; known in Cyprus
why.stewardship: Stavros Papastavrou, US-based Cypriot businessman, owns the football company since 2018
why.women: Has a women's football department; level not covered (estimate)

why.terrace: B-kozep and Green Monsters ultras; Hungary's best-known support, Green Brothers alliance with Rapid Wien
why.city: Budapest's most popular club, rooted in the 9th district
why.voice: Run by a president; fans' 2014-16 boycott over scanners ended in talks, little formal influence
why.conscience: UEFA fined EUR 15,000 and closed part of the stadium for supporters' racist behaviour v Slovan Bratislava (2022); earlier 2014 racism sanction
why.ground: Groupama Arena (23,700), modern 2014 ground in the 9th district
why.contender: 36 league titles incl. a long run to 2024-25; 2nd in 2025-26, 2026 cup
why.rituals: Green-white, eagle mascot, well-known choreos in Hungary
why.stewardship: President Gabor Kubatov, Fidesz politician, since 2011; club closely tied to the governing party
why.women: Women's section exists and has won Hungarian titles (estimate)

why.terrace: Kanarifansen (1992), 5,000+ members, Norway's second-largest fan club
why.city: The town of Lillestrom's club; 'Kanarifugla' are central to local identity
why.voice: Norwegian member club (sports associations keep majority control; estimate)
why.ground: Arasen (12,250), compact, record 13,652; best season average 9,018 (2007)
why.contender: Relegated 2024, unbeaten 1. divisjon and Norwegian Cup 2025, 5th in 2026
why.rituals: Canary yellow, Kanarifansen songs; known in Norway (estimate)
why.stewardship: Member club with local investors; no outside owner found
why.women: LSK Kvinner, alliance club with 7 Toppserien titles (2012-19), 4th in 2025

why.terrace: Sector G ultras (1990); one of Bulgaria's two biggest followings
why.city: Sofia's army club, sharing the capital with Levski
why.voice: Privately owned; no formal supporter power found
why.conscience: UEFA fined EUR 50,000 plus ticket ban in July 2026 for fans' Nazi salutes at Derry City; bananas thrown at Black players 2022
why.ground: Temporarily at the Vasil Levski national stadium (running track) while the Bulgarian Army Stadium is rebuilt
why.contender: 4th in 2025-26, 2026 cup and supercup; last title 2008
why.rituals: Red star crest, Eternal Derby with Levski; known in Bulgaria
why.stewardship: Walter Papazki took control Dec 2025 after Fond Sport (Grisha Ganchev era) handed him its shares; brand dispute with CSKA 1948

why.terrace: F-Side (1976) and VAK410 stand all match; 94,000-member supporters club
why.city: Amsterdam's club and the Netherlands' most supported
why.voice: Members' association Vereniging AFC Ajax holds about 73% of the listed company
why.conscience: Repeated UEFA fines for crowd disturbances incl. objects thrown at the Bernabeu (2025-26) and F-Side linked to rioting
why.ground: Johan Cruyff Arena (55,865), large roofed bowl, well filled
why.rituals: 'Three Little Birds', Jewish-identity chants by fans; known worldwide
why.stewardship: Members' association majority, listed on Euronext; NN Group 5%
why.women: Ajax Vrouwen in the Eredivisie since 2012 with league and cup titles
why.intensity: Total Football heritage; recent sides mixed (Farioli's more cautious 2024-25)

why.terrace: Vak P ultras; loud, organised and known in the Netherlands
why.city: Enschede's club and the region's 'Trots van het Oosten'
why.ground: De Grolsch Veste (30,205), club-owned, usually well filled
why.rituals: Crowd sings 'You'll Never Walk Alone' before every kick-off
why.stewardship: Club-run, chaired by Dominique Scholten; bankrupt 2003 and KNVB sanctions 2015-16 after mismanagement
why.women: FC Twente Vrouwen: 10 national titles incl. 2024 and 2025, 2026 cup; club's first women's section
